newsitem.title: CHINA: China says U.S. concerns on rights, HK unneccesary.
newsitem.headline: China says U.S. concerns on rights, HK unneccesary.

text.p: China on Wednesday dismissed concerns raised by U.S. President Bill Clinton over human rights and Hong Kong by crowing its success in rights protection and vowing full future freedom for residents of the British colony.

"The national conditions of China and the United States are not the same and it is natural for different views on human rights to exist," a Chinese Foreign Ministry spokeswoman said in reaction to comments by Clinton on Tuesday.
Clinton said Washington had made less progress than hoped on bringing about change in China's human rights policy but defended his policy of constructive engagement toward Beijing.

On Hong Kong, Clinton said the British colony might prove to be of less value to China if the civil liberties of its people were crushed after London returns the territory to Beijing rule at midnight on June 30.

Beijing had guaranteed the freedoms of the people of Hong Kong by issuing its Basic Law, a mini-constitution, for the territory and concerns on the issue were unfounded, the Chinese Foreign Ministry spokeswoman said.
"Under the Basic Law the people of Hong Kong have full freedom and all democratic rights," she said. "There is no basis or need for doubt or concern about this."

On human rights, an issue of dispute that has long strained sensitive Sino-U.S. ties, China's constitution and laws protected the rights of members of all its nationalities and Beijing's record spoke for itself, she said.
"The efforts and achievements made by the Chinese government in this area are there for all to see," she said. "Anyone who is not biased will reach a fair conclusion."
A U.S. delegation arrived in Beijing on Tuesday for talks on human rights with Chinese officials, after a year that saw the imprisonment or exile of virtually every political dissident.
The Chinese spokeswoman said Beijing believed talks on such issues should take the overall situation of ties into account and should be carried out on a basis of equality.
"Only in this way can we improve understanding and benefit the healthy development of ties between the two countries," she said.
